groups.passage:
**Retailer opens small fulfillment hub near downtown**

Home goods retailer Birch & Lane has opened a 9,000-square-foot fulfillment hub inside a renovated industrial building near downtown. The site stores the company’s 600 fastest-selling products and handles same-day orders from nearby neighborhoods. Larger furniture still ships from the regional warehouse.

The company selected the smaller site after delivery data showed that nearly half of local online orders contained only one or two compact items. By placing those products closer to customers, Birch & Lane expects to shorten van routes and reduce repeated trips across the city.

The hub will operate for a one-year trial. The retailer will compare delivery time, vehicle mileage, and staffing cost before deciding whether to open a second site.

questions.question_text: What products are stored at the new hub?
The word “compact” is closest in meaning to
Why did Birch & Lane choose a smaller downtown site?

options.text: Many local orders contain only a few small items.
The regional warehouse is closing immediately.
The site has space for every product.

questions.question_text: What will influence whether a second hub opens?

options.text: The number of industrial buildings in another country
A change in store opening hours

groups.passage:
**Production schedule – Line B**

Monday: Product R, 6 A.M.–2 P.M.
Tuesday: Product S, 6 A.M.–noon; cleaning noon–2 P.M.
Wednesday: Product T, 7 A.M.–3 P.M.
Thursday: Product R, 6 A.M.–2 P.M.

---

**Maintenance request M-88**
Submitted Tuesday 9:20 A.M.
Issue: temperature sensor gives intermittent high readings
Estimated repair: 45 minutes
Machine can continue operating if technician verifies readings manually every 20 minutes.

---

**Manager message 9:35 A.M.**

Please keep Product S running until noon with the manual checks described in M-88. Schedule the sensor repair during the cleaning period so we do not lose production time. If the repair exceeds 45 minutes, cleaning may continue around the technician, but Product T must not start Wednesday until the sensor test passes.

questions.question_text: What is Line B producing when M-88 is submitted?
When should the sensor repair begin?
How can production continue before the repair?

options.text: By checking sensor readings manually every 20 minutes
By turning off the sensor completely
By moving Product S to Line A

questions.question_text: What condition must be met before Product T starts?

options.text: The sensor must pass a test.
The technician must leave the building.

questions.question_text: What can be inferred about the manager’s plan?

options.text: It is intended to minimize lost production time.
It moves all maintenance to Thursday.
It assumes the sensor cannot be repaired.
